$comment: Authored short forms of each card's counter-move, compressed from the source's own Counter-Move Defense block. They print on the card back; the full block prints in the rules and skill artifacts. A short form may drop explanation but may not add a claim, change a number, or omit a stated bound.

defenses.NEG-01: Name the attribution: if personal capability were the bottleneck, replacing me would clear the containers today.
defenses.NEG-02: Re-anchor to governance: liquidity preservation is mandated; benchmarks are open, termination protection is not.
defenses.NEG-03: Dispute the index's method: it counts waterfront properties unlike ours; ask for a normalized comparable dataset.
defenses.NEG-04: Reframe their criteria: their offer buys base pay now; ours buys long-term equity in a market-dominant ecosystem.
defenses.NEG-05: Affirm the internal alternative: engineering has costed the architecture, two sprint teams and maintenance overhead.
defenses.NEG-06: Redirect from multiples to substance: 140% net revenue retention and zero churn before fixing a valuation bracket.
defenses.NEG-07: Enforce the package: $180,000 is contingent on prepayment and case studies; unbundled, the fee returns to $230,000.
defenses.NEG-08: Refuse the contingency: it rewards short-term velocity over brand; require a predictable fee-for-service model.
defenses.NEG-09: Keep brainstorming exploratory: require a bilateral memorandum that concepts discussed stay uncommitted.
defenses.NEG-10: Defend the signed contract: do not reopen core terms under the rubric of post-settlement optimization.
defenses.NEG-11: Before discussing margin, ask which service-level provisions they would eliminate in exchange for fee reductions.
defenses.NEG-12: Name the claim, not the feeling: it is a breach under Section 8.2; turn to the contractual remediation provisions.
defenses.NEG-13: Yes, unprecedented in our vendor tier: uncapped IP indemnity for third-party open source violates our risk charter.
defenses.NEG-14: Acknowledge the audit and press the facts: listing frustrations does not offset an unforecasted 20% cost increase.
defenses.NEG-15: Return the burden: the codebase separates core platform modules from tenant logic; we will show the schematic.
defenses.NEG-16: Agreement is not consent: acknowledging the history does not accept the migration proposal; examine downtime metrics.
defenses.NEG-17: Acknowledge the pause and hold: take whatever time you need; I am ready to explore the underlying economics.
defenses.NEG-18: Name the cost of the cadence: downtime runs at $50,000 per hour; we need urgent action, not vocal pacing.
defenses.NEG-19: Recognize the hook and ask for the basis: what specific budgetary data points led you to that hypothesis?
defenses.NEG-20: Reject the binary: neither model fits; require a hybrid that automates API monitoring without weekly manual work.
defenses.NEG-21: Respect alignment, name the runway: three months left; review capital reallocation terms now, relational dynamics after.
defenses.NEG-22: Board seats and keynotes do not offset cash flow; require a direct, verifiable cut in capital expenditure.
defenses.NEG-23: Reject the anchor: $750,000 is outside allocation; wipe it from the table and price baseline developer-day rates.
defenses.NEG-24: Isolate the target: the $1.4M configuration is irrelevant here; judge the $340,000 proposal on its own economics.
defenses.NEG-25: Attack the boundary: we do not peg pay to speculative ranges; the approved band for this tier caps at $215,000.
defenses.NEG-26: Strip the illusion: $347,850 rests on subjective hour assumptions; round to a ceiling and examine the day rates.
defenses.NEG-27: Name the schedule: diminishing adjustments are internal pricing, not our ceiling; our limit is $170,000, not $187,500.
defenses.NEG-28: Name the curve: this is the Ackerman sequence; the final figure is still below our cost of delivery; restructure scope.
defenses.NEG-29: Deflect the loss frame: legacy maintenance is provisioned; do not accelerate procurement on hypothetical loss models.
defenses.NEG-30: Expose the decoy: Tier 2 is unviable on purpose; strip insurance and extra connectors and price Tier 2 at $135,000.
defenses.NEG-31: Hold the midpoint: if it cannot be met, revert to a granular cost audit and delay launch by two months.
defenses.NEG-32: Stand by the deadline: implementation capacity closes today; unpaid at 5:00 PM, those engineers go to another client.
defenses.NEG-33: Tie past to performance: spend rested on milestones you missed; future commitments cannot be separated from them.
defenses.NEG-34: Answer directly: no, the initiative is not abandoned; capital priority moved to data migration, re-engagement in Q3.
defenses.NEG-35: This is not hypothetical: the board has fixed this expenditure cap; institutional authority does not extend beyond it.
defenses.NEG-36: Reframe the nibble: support is part of core delivery; treating it as an add-on questions the partnership integrity.
defenses.NEG-37: Answer the naming: not strategic; our security review found new compliance hurdles we must address under the charter.
defenses.NEG-38: Neutralize the flinch: name the surprise, then walk the cost model, risk allocations and compliance guarantees.
defenses.NEG-39: Split the coalition: your CFO holds the cash line, you see the long-term value; equip you to show the ROI justifies it.
defenses.NEG-40: Bound the risk: a pre-mortem is prudent, but speculation cannot paralyze commitments; fix the bounds with explicit SLAs.
defenses.NEG-41: Name the bogey: removing a meeting does not offset accelerated net-30 terms; evaluate those terms on their own merits.
defenses.NEG-42: Answer fairness with evidence: it is measured by comparable transactions and shared margin risk; review the rate cards.
defenses.NEG-43: Stand by the price: brief the committee jointly, and hold the current pricing structure through that discussion.
defenses.NEG-44: Respect the walk-away: the door remains open if parameters change; wish their secondary acquisition success.
